question: Does an actually integrated trace translation kernel lower complete prime-field solving cost relative to the matched native baseline and strongest registered rho?
hypotheses: If the affected translation phase has nonzero measured share f and speedup s, total speedup follows 1/((1-f)+f/s), with new setup and recovery charged.
The current incidence path makes no trace-kernel calls, so its recorded runtime cannot inherit that component ratio.

inputs.primary_scope: one public target at a time; aggregate panels are secondary

reference.selection: Use the cheapest registered protocol-matched reference, including applicable automorphisms. Tune cold overhead on separate qualification inputs before held-out comparisons; do not select a post-hoc best seed.
reference.adapter_gap: Aggregate engine timer only; exclusive walk/collision/recovery intervals still required for admission.

charged_work: public mixed-label generation including rejected draws
translation including collisions and exceptional points
retry_policy: fixed seed order; stop at first informative relation, retain preceding costs; four misses are censored, not a completed solve
controls: dense and trace translations on identical native backend

admission.backend: isolab EKS Spot with native L2
admission.budget_note: Proposal only. Includes build, idle, failed and interrupted attempts; launch requires an authorized finite balance covering all of them.
admission.outputs: approved S3 custody, all raw records, independent replay and recompute; PCC standing before promotion

blocking_dependencies: confirm live monthly and daily headroom
compile and test native rho adapter
replace relevant historical Python execution paths with native code
integrate trace translation into an execution path that actually uses divisor translation
complete phase instrumentation and matched reference qualification
claim_boundary: No measured ratio to rho, new arithmetic exponent or extrapolation to 256-bit/binary fields is asserted.
